name: Form
purpose: Lay out a set of fields the user fills in and submits together - a native <form> with a header, grouped/rowed fields, and a footer of actions.
intent: Be a thin layout organism, not a form-state manager. Figma's Form is pure layout + slots, and this system already puts labelling/description/validation on Field and native behaviour on the control - so Form renders a real <form> (native submission + validation for free), an optional header, and the section/row/footer spacing, and owns no form state. Composes molecules (Field and its controls) into a complete UI section, so it lives at the organism tier.

subParts.name: code-parts / <form-header>
subParts.note: Title (heading/lg) + description (body/md, the '*' in content/error) + optional content slot. Props: show title, show description, show content (default false), title, description. Rendered in code from Form's title/description/requiredLegend props (baked into Form, not a separate export).

subParts.name: code-parts / <form-section>
subParts.note: Vertical group: optional heading (heading/sm, showTitle default false) + form-rows. padding-top spacing/3xl, internal gap spacing/lg. Rendered in code as FormSection.

subParts.name: code-parts / <form-row>
subParts.note: 1-4 equal-width slots side by side (variant 'number of slots'), each holding a Field, with a spacing/lg gap between them. Rendered in code as FormRow (equal columns via flex).

subParts.name: code-parts / <form-footer>
subParts.note: Actions slot aligned start/end (align variant). padding-top spacing/4xl, action gap spacing/sm. Rendered in code as FormFooter.

apiAdaptationNotes: The Figma Form page is still marked work-in-progress (🚧). The <form-row> column gap was initially unset (0); it has since been set to --spacing-lg (16px) in Figma, matching what the code already used, so it is no longer a judgment call. One call remains: the header title is a Figma text node, so `title` renders as presentational text, not a semantic heading.
Figma's `sections` variant (1/2/3) is not a prop - it is just however many FormSection children the consumer renders.

The <form-header> is always the form's own header, so it is baked into Form (title/description/requiredLegend props) rather than a separate export. The description's '* indicates a required field' legend is exposed as the `requiredLegend` boolean, rendering the '*' in --color-content-error to match Field's required marker.
Multi-part component shipped as four separate exports (Form, FormSection, FormRow, FormFooter), matching the repo's Tabs/TabPanel and RadioGroup/Radio pattern rather than dot-notation compounds.
All inter-block spacing lives on the blocks (section padding-top 3xl, footer padding-top 4xl); the <form> has no gap of its own, so a header-less form has no wasted leading space.

Fields may sit directly in a FormSection (single column, spaced by the section gap) or inside a FormRow (equal columns) - Figma always nests rows in sections, but the direct-field case is the common one and avoids a mandatory one-slot row.
Form owns no form state - it renders a native <form> and forwards onSubmit and all native form attributes; validation and each field's state stay native / on Field.

useCases: a titled single-section create form with an end-aligned submit
a form with two- or three-up rows of related fields
antiPatterns: a single standalone control (use Field or the bare control)
a page section that isn't a form (use plain layout)
managing per-field validation state in Form (that's Field / the native control)

anatomy.description: The form element; forwards ref and native form attributes. Renders the optional header, then children.
Rendered when title, description, or requiredLegend is set. flex column, gap --spacing-md.
Header description and/or the required legend, --typography-body-md, --color-content-default.
The legend '*', --color-content-error. Real content (not aria-hidden) - the sentence explains the convention.
Vertical field group; padding-top --spacing-3xl, gap --spacing-lg; optional title (--typography-heading-sm).
Equal-width columns on one line (up to 4); gap --spacing-lg; each child flex:1 1 0.
Actions; padding-top --spacing-4xl, gap --spacing-sm; data-align end (default) / start.

title.description: Header title (heading/lg). Presentational text - not a semantic heading.

requiredLegend.description: Renders the '* indicates a required field' legend, with the '*' in the error colour.

children.description: The form body: FormSection / FormRow groups and a FormFooter.

headerClassName.description: Composes with the header's class list.

className.description: Composes with the form element's class list.

...rest.description: Forwarded to the native <form> (onSubmit, name, noValidate, ...).

titleClassName.description: Composes with the title's class list.

children.description: Up to 4 fields, laid out as equal-width columns.
Action Buttons - typically Cancel + a submit.

requirements: Render a real native <form> - native submission (Enter, type=submit) and browser validation work for free.
Give the submit Button type='submit' so it triggers onSubmit.
Field owns each control's labelling and description - Form does not re-wire them.
The section title is presentational; add a semantic heading in the page structure if a group needs one.
The required legend (including its '*') is real content, not aria-hidden.

keyboardInteraction: Native form behaviour - Tab between fields; Enter in a field submits; a type='submit' button submits.
Form itself has no custom keyboard handling.
behaviorRules: Render a native <form>; forward ref and native form attributes (onSubmit, name, noValidate, ...).
Render the header only when title, description, or requiredLegend is set.
requiredLegend renders '* indicates a required field' with the '*' in --color-content-error.
Spacing lives on the blocks (section padding-top 3xl, footer padding-top 4xl); the <form> has gap 0.
FormSection adds --spacing-3xl top spacing and spaces its children by --spacing-lg; title optional.
FormRow lays its children out as equal-width columns (flex:1 1 0), gap --spacing-lg.
FormFooter defaults to align='end'; align='start' left-aligns; gap --spacing-sm between actions.
Support className on every part (plus headerClassName / titleClassName).
compositionRules: Use Field for each control; Form arranges Fields, it does not replace them.
Wrap 2-4 side-by-side fields in a FormRow; place a full-width field directly in a FormSection.
Group related fields in a FormSection; give it a title only when the group needs a heading.
Put the actions in a FormFooter and give the submit Button type='submit'.
contentRules: Title is a short noun phrase; description is a concise supporting line.
Use requiredLegend when any field in the form is required, so the '*' has an explanation.
responsiveRules: The form fills its container's inline size; a FormRow's columns share the width equally.
themeRules: Must work in light and dark themes - all colours use semantic tokens.
implementationNotes: Form uses React.memo + React.forwardRef<HTMLFormElement>; the sub-parts use React.memo.
No hardcoded colours, spacing, radius, or typography.
Ship four separate exports (Form, FormSection, FormRow, FormFooter), not dot-notation compounds.
do: Render a real <form> and let native submission/validation work.
Use Field for each control and arrange them with FormSection / FormRow.
Use requiredLegend when the form has required fields.
dont: Don't manage per-field validation state in Form - that's Field / the native control.
Don't use Form for a single standalone control or a non-form page section.
Don't rely on the section title as a semantic heading - it's presentational.
Don't put more than 4 fields in one FormRow.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders a native <form>; forwards its ref and native attributes (onSubmit, name, noValidate).
Renders the header from title / description / requiredLegend; the legend shows a coloured '*' reading '* indicates a required field'; no header renders when all three are absent.
FormSection renders an optional title and adds --spacing-3xl top spacing.
FormRow lays its children out as equal-width columns.
FormFooter defaults to align='end' and supports align='start' via data-align.
Composes className on every part (plus headerClassName / titleClassName).
Uses only semantic tokens; works in light and dark themes.
Storybook includes Playground, Repository, Sections, Rows, FooterAlignment, and EdgeCases.
Tests cover the native form + submit + ref/attrs, header/legend, sections, rows, and footer alignment.
knownLimitations: Figma source is work-in-progress (🚧): the presentational (non-heading) title is provisional.
No built-in responsive collapse of multi-column rows on narrow containers.
Form manages no form state or validation - it is layout + a native <form> only.
futureEnhancements: Opt-in responsive stacking of FormRow columns on narrow containers.
A semantic-heading option for the title / section titles once the design settles.
